narrative:
On November 26, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 2,601 cases across 50 judges and conducted hearings for 928, yielding an overall hearing rate of 35.7%. This reflects a slight drop in judicial throughput compared to recent daily performance, down from 38.8% (1,018 of 2,622) on November 25, 39.0% (1,062 of 2,723) on November 24, and 38.4% (1,118 of 2,912) on November 23.

Judge-level metrics varied across cause lists. Bench listings featuring the Chief Justice & K.S. Hemalekha saw up to 93.8% clearance (15 of 16 heard), while G Basavaraja in Hall 32 achieved 67.2% (41 of 61) and C.M. Poonacha cleared 65.0% (52 of 80) on his primary list. Conversely, certain cause lists saw zero conversions, including Suraj Govindaraj (0 of 130 across lists) and E.S. Indiresch (0 of 19). Stage conversion analysis shows that procedural matters dominated efficiency: Orders cases reached a 39.9% hearing rate (339 of 849), while Admission matters saw 40.3% conversion (265 of 658), improving from 32.5% on the prior day. Final Hearing matters recorded a lower conversion of 19.8% (106 of 535), down from 27.4% on November 25.

Regarding subject matter distribution, Writ Petitions (WP) formed the bulk of the docket with 882 cases scheduled and 276 heard (31.3%), reflecting a marginal dip from November 25 (34.4%). Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) followed with 522 scheduled and 205 heard (39.3%), down from 50.9% yesterday. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) saw a minor rise in conversion to 36.0% (154 of 428 heard compared to 33.5% on November 25). Higher conversion rates were concentrated in specific categories such as Civil Miscellaneous Petitions (CMP) at 58.9% (43 of 73) and Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) at 55.2% (53 of 96).
